bull.b: A $3.5B ARR base growing 25% YoY reflects durable subscription economics and a large, sticky customer footprint. High ARR supports predictable revenue, recurring cash flow and upsell potential across ZIA/ZPA modules, enabling multi-year visibility into growth and renewal-driven profitability.

Consistently ~80% gross margins indicate strong platform economics from a cloud-native, multi-tenant security model. High gross margins provide structural operating leverage as revenue scales, enabling investment in R&D and go-to-market while preserving room for durable operating margin expansion over time.

Robust FCF (over $1.0B TTM) and rising operating cash flow are durable strengths that fund organic investment, tuck-in M&A (e.g., Red Canary, Symmetry Systems) and debt reduction. Strong cash conversion gives management flexibility to scale infrastructure and strategic initiatives without heavy external financing.

bear.b: Despite improving margins and cash flow, persistent GAAP losses and negative ROE show the company has not yet delivered enduring accounting profitability. This limits reinvestment efficiency, can constrain investor confidence, and means long-term returns depend on sustaining margin gains and turning net income positive.

Management's early FY27 outlook (16%–17% growth) and implied organic net new ARR slowdown reduce expected top-line leverage. Slower growth can compress future margin expansion, make it harder to justify higher fixed costs, and raises execution risk to sustain large-account and cross-sell momentum.

Management expects higher, persistent CapEx driven by AI/data center demand and pull-forward purchases. Increased capital intensity and component price pressure can structurally lower free cash flow margins, raise asset intensity and require ongoing investment to sustain performance at scale.
